papers.title: Effect of heat treatment on corrosion behaviour of selective laser melted Ti-6Al-4V alloy in Ringer's solution
papers.abstract: The additive manufacturing is developing rapidly among the advanced technologies to fabricate the orthopaedic and dental implants with complex shape (e.g. spherical) due to such advantages as high production efficiency and minimal waste of material. Ti-6Al-4V alloy samples were fabricated by the technology of selective laser melting. The effect of a post heat treatment, carried out below the polymorphic transformation temperature, on the microstructure and corrosion behaviour of the alloy was investigated. It was determined that such a heat treatment of the microstructure leads to improving corrosion resistance of Ti-6Al-4V alloy in Ringer's solution due to a growth of the β phase, an decrease of the α' martensite and microstrain in the α/α' lattice. • Ti-6Al-4V alloy samples were manufactured by selective laser melting technology. • Heat treatment led to improving corrosion resistance of alloy in Ringer's solution. • This is associated with growth of β phase and decrease of α' martensite.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了热处理对选区激光熔化Ti-6Al-4V合金腐蚀行为的影响，但未涉及力学性能，与方向关注的疲劳/力学性能不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not report any mechanical performance metrics such as fatigue life, tensile strength, or porosity closure; it focuses solely on corrosion behavior.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of sub-transus heat treatment on the corrosion behavior of selective laser melted Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V samples were fabricated by selective laser melting and subjected to heat treatment below the polymorphic transformation temperature, followed by microstructural characterization and corrosion testing in Ringer's solution.
summary_en.result: Heat treatment improved corrosion resistance due to increased β phase fraction and reduced α' martensite and microstrain.
summary_en.validation: Corrosion resistance was evaluated using electrochemical tests in Ringer's solution.
